payload: {"schema":1,"version":"0.0.56","date":"2026-11-01","lede":"Merging clay layers no longer leaves missing patches up close","highlights":["Merged clay layers are complete up close","Smooth Boolean / Merge of rotated layers","Align moves only the clicked clay primitive","Brush value drag on left / middle mouse"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.56","windows":{"url":"https://github.com/c6ank/klay-releases/releases/download/0.0.56/Klay_Setup_0.0.56.exe","size":408218466,"sha512":"2622c96a3a1a1372bc6291d998a44ca8f62ac54a7cc67052eba178e2cb0411897f79c1faf35af33c1445b31abdb2f5b78aa031e7959a9d6a51d663c3341cdd24"},"mac":{"version":"0.0.56","url":"https://github.com/c6ank/klay-releases/releases/download/0.0.56/Klay_0.0.56_macOS.dmg","size":530851618,"sha512":"7007663be6d3a740381d7e83612ddc780654399e89d473adc2c7ac0bddcbafbba11edc97012162cc4907088d981a02a6d9c754e1d7823d26cf065d6fe66d7aee"},"items":[{"g":"f","t":"Merging two clay layers, or uniting them with Boolean, could leave missing patches of surface that showed only up close. The merged layer is now complete."},{"g":"f","t":"A clay Boolean or Merge of a rotated or rescaled layer could leave pinholes and short raised lines along the voxel grid. The result is now smooth and closed."},{"g":"f","t":"The Align tool now moves only the clay primitive you click, as it does an object, instead of the whole clay layer that holds it. Two primitives of the same clay layer can also be aligned onto each other."},{"g":"f","t":"On clay layers, resizing the Smooth brush while holding Shift now keeps the new size after Shift is released, when the Smooth brush uses the primary brush size."}],"history":[{"version":"0.0.55","date":"2026-11-01","lede":"Faster, lighter clay: sculpting up to 5x faster on half the memory; a Primitives tool with 133 parametric shapes for Poly and Clay; Color correct looks in the Library; Smooth or Handles curves with a live dab preview; Sharp retopology hits its polycount with clean open borders","highlights":["Faster, lighter clay","Primitives tool","Point instancing in instance packs","Clay layer resolution","Color correct looks","More ways to blend clay"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.55","items":[{"g":"n","t":"Faster, lighter clay","b":"Clay sculpting is up to four to five times faster and a clay object uses about half the video memory, so larger and more detailed clay fits on the same card. Large strokes now release without a pause.","w":["Clay layers"]},{"g":"n","t":"Primitives tool","b":"A new Primitives tool places 133 parametric shapes, from boxes, gears and knots to rocks, architecture parts and fractals, as a poly mesh or as clay. Click places a shape on the surface and handles adjust its size and parameters; the card adds deform, symmetry, surface noise and boolean settings, plus a Box mode for shaping a cube and a Lasso mode that inflates a drawn outline. On a clay layer each shape is listed in the outliner, where its blend, order and grouping can be edited.","w":["Tools \u203a Primitives"]},{"g":"n","t":"Point instancing in instance packs","b":"An instance pack holds copies of one or more objects as points, far beyond the previous limit of about a thousand copies per scene, and draws them faster than the same number of separate copies. Instance point adds the selection as a point to the current pack, or creates a pack when there is none; move the new point and press it again within five seconds to repeat the move. Create > Instance pack makes an empty pack and Add to pack chooses the target pack, the outliner lists each object of a pack with its own visibility, and a single point can be selected, moved, duplicated or removed. Packs work with poly and clay objects, shadows and the path tracer, and Ctrl+D still makes a separate copy.","w":["Right-click \u203a Copy \u203a Instance point"]},{"g":"n","t":"Clay layer resolution","b":"Each clay layer has a resolution of Low, Default, High, Ultra or Extreme, chosen from the capsule beside its name in the outliner, which also shows the layer's scale in its colour. Clay layers now also show a rendered thumbnail on their outliner card, like poly meshes, refreshed when you switch to another layer. A higher resolution gives a bigger box at the same detail; Extreme is meant for graphics cards with plenty of memory, a lower one cuts the clay outside the smaller box after asking first, and Undo restores it.","w":["Outliner \u203a Clay layer \u203a Resolution"]},{"g":"n","t":"Color correct looks","b":"The Library has a Color correct category of saved looks, each shown on the same grey sphere so they compare side by side. Click a look to apply it to the Post process; turn off Click applies to select with a click and apply with a double-click. Every Color correct panel (Post, the Camera Grade panel and the picture viewer) now has Copy, Paste and Save at the top, and shows the name of the look last applied.","w":["Library \u203a Color correct"]},{"g":"n","t":"More ways to blend clay","b":"The clay Boolean panel's Blending section adds Inset, Extrude, Line groove, Tongue, Repel and Avoid, which press, raise or engrave one object into another or make the objects give way to each other. A folded More blends section holds twelve further joins: Columns, Stairs, Pipe and Split edge for hard surfaces, Noisy, Sag, Stretch and Bridge for organic joins, and Exclude, Morph, Shell and Replace. A Type switch under the tiles sets how every join is rounded: Smooth, Chamfer, or, from the \u22ef button, Soft, Circular, Silky and Exact. The same joins and types are available on the shapes of a clay layer made with the Primitives tool, from the outliner's Join card, whose Blending section can be folded to keep only the Union, Subtract and Intersect switch, and from the right-click Join menu.","w":["Boolean \u203a Clay \u203a Blending"]},{"g":"n","t":"Zen toolbar","b":"A compact, icon-only bottom toolbar: the round dot at the right end of the toolbar switches to it, the short bar at its right end switches back, and Ctrl+T (Cmd+T on macOS) switches between the two. Names and shortcuts appear on hover, and the brush drawer and the tools list open above it. Drag either arrow sideways to show more or fewer brushes or tools; hold a brush or a tool to drag it to a new place, as on the full toolbar. The full toolbar's brush arrow, and a new arrow on its Tools card, resize the same way.","w":["Bottom toolbar \u203a Zen toolbar"]},{"g":"n","t":"Brush pastille","b":"An optional column on the left of the viewport for the Zen toolbar, turned on by right-clicking the toolbar: Radius and Strength sit at the top, followed by any functions, brush settings, Stamp, Falloff, Stencil, dividers, switches and folders you add with Add function. Right-click the pastille to add, reorder or remove items.","w":["Zen toolbar \u203a right-click \u203a Brush pastille"]},{"g":"n","t":"Folds growth for stamp brushes","b":"The stamp brush's Growth section has a Branches | Folds switch. With Folds, holding the brush on a clay layer grows a folded, organic surface from a small ball or from the clay under the brush. The clay itself changes smoothly at frame rate while you hold, at a steady pace that does not depend on the frame rate (about seven seconds to the Stop at size), with folds kept thick enough that the surface stays closed, and releasing it keeps the result as one undo step; Esc during the hold restores the clay. Grown from the clay under the brush, the folds become the clay's own surface, with no second surface left underneath, so they can also turn inward into the clay; grown from a ball, the growth is added onto the clay. Dragging the brush seeds new growth along the whole stroke, anywhere on the layer, at the brush's spacing. The new Frill, Lettuce, Coral, Fine coral, Brain and Swell stamp brushes are set up for it. Settle after freezes older growth away from the growing edges so it no longer counts toward Max points, which lets the edges keep growing during long holds.","w":["Brush \u203a Growth \u203a Folds"]},{"g":"n","t":"Volume texture for clay brushes","b":"Any clay brush can project a grayscale image through the clay with triplanar mapping, on top of what the brush already does. Strength sets how much it acts. Add raises the light parts and sinks the dark ones, Carve only digs the dark parts in, and Break cuts the brush's own deposit where the image is dark, so the stroke lands as broken chunks. Map, Triplanar and Cells offer the same controls as the Flood tab's Displace texture.","w":["Brush \u203a Noise & patterns \u203a Volume texture"]},{"g":"n","t":"Crease and rake in clay","b":"The clay Elastique brush can now crease and rake clay live: drag across the surface to fold the clay ahead of the brush and leave a clean groove behind it, from a soft valley to a knife-sharp crease or a raised ridge. The groove's profile, depth and width respond to pen pressure, and Slide warp lets the surface stretch and bunch around it like skin. Holding Ctrl, or turning on Invert brush, raises the same profile out of the surface instead of cutting it. Dab length sets how often the groove is laid down, so a shorter step follows quick turns closely.","w":["Brush \u203a Elastique \u203a Surface slide"]},{"g":"n","t":"Poly brushes in the Clay tab","b":"Right-click a brush in the toolbar's Poly tab and choose Copy to Clay preset to add a copy of it to the Clay tab, where it sculpts clay layers with the same behaviour. The copy is a separate preset: changing its settings does not affect the original brush.","w":["Toolbar \u203a Poly \u203a right-click \u203a Copy to Clay preset"]},{"g":"n","t":"Smooth or Handles curves","b":"Every curve editor has a Smooth | Handles switch under the graph. Smooth keeps the current behaviour. Handles draws B\u00e9zier segments whose handles follow the points automatically; drag a handle to bend that point by hand, and right-click the handle to make it automatic again. Points and handles highlight under the cursor. The mode and any bent handles are saved with each curve. The area under the curve is now filled, and the brush Falloff curve shows a live preview of the dab above it that updates while you drag a point.","w":["Brush \u203a Falloff curve"]},{"g":"f","t":"The gizmo now scales a clay layer evenly on all three axes. Scaling a clay layer along one axis, which distorted the clay, is no longer offered."},{"g":"f","t":"The installer no longer refuses to install when an earlier Klay was removed by deleting its folder. It now clears the leftover entry and continues, and if an earlier version cannot be uninstalled it offers to install over it."},{"g":"f","t":"In VR through Virtual Desktop, the headset image no longer looks darker than the viewport. If another VR runtime shows the headset too dark or too bright, the VR window's Headset output setting changes how the image is handed to it."},{"g":"f","t":"A Laser cut with fill through parts that pass into each other, such as fingers resting on a palm, crossing strands or an unmerged sculpt, now fills each part cleanly. The fill previously could leave holes or flipped faces at the seam. These cuts are also faster."},{"g":"f","t":"After many Move strokes on a clay object, patches of the surface no longer disappear where you pulled. They previously stayed missing until a Smooth stroke passed over them."},{"g":"f","t":"The clay Elastique brush now shows its Compressibility while you drag, so the surface no longer shifts slightly when you release."},{"g":"f","t":"With symmetry on, the dot that marks the mirrored brush position is now hidden when it is behind the model."},{"g":"f","t":"The Mirror tool's cut keeps quads where the mirror plane crosses a row of quads. The centre seam previously became a strip of triangles."},{"g":"f","t":"Sharp retopology now produces close to the polycount you set. It previously gave about a third of the target on the starter head (around 1,900 faces for 5,000)."},{"g":"f","t":"After a gizmo Align, scaling along one axis no longer distorts the model and no longer makes the gizmo disappear. Align now turns the green axis to the picked face."},{"g":"f","t":"Undoing or redoing a gizmo move, rotation or scale now brings the gizmo back with the object. It previously stayed where the drag had ended."},{"g":"f","t":"Selecting with V now works on clay objects the same way as on poly: a drag box selects every clay object it covers, a single one becomes the active layer, and a V click no longer creates a new clay layer."},{"g":"f","t":"After a Boolean between a clay object and a poly mesh, deleting another clay object no longer leaves a copy of the used clay object in the viewport that could not be selected in the outliner or deleted. Undo now also restores that clay object correctly."},{"g":"f","t":"Redo after undoing a Laser cut on a clay object now restores the cut exactly. It could previously bring back a damaged surface."},{"g":"f","t":"Voxelize now shows only the finished result, with its detail projected. The bare voxel shell no longer appears for a moment before the detail."},{"g":"f","t":"Favourites in the library are no longer limited: pinning a new one no longer removes the oldest. Clicking the Stamp or Falloff tile on the toolbar shows every favourite in a grid."},{"g":"f","t":"On a narrow Library window the header buttons no longer run under the Size slider: Import, Save current, Click applies and Re-render all now sit on their own row under the header, with Size at its right."},{"g":"f","t":"The Library button in the top bar now reopens the Library on the category you last used, including after a restart. It previously always opened on Clay stamps."},{"g":"f","t":"Video memory is released after you subdivide a mesh to a high level. About 1 GB used to stay reserved for the rest of the session, even after a new scene or with only a small model left."},{"g":"f","t":"Boolean and Blend results on clay objects now keep each object's surface smooth. The preview and the applied result could previously show blocky bumps over the whole surface, away from the join."},{"g":"f","t":"With symmetry on, clay brushes with Elastique or Surface slide now warp both sides as mirror images and no longer drag clay across the symmetry plane."}]},{"version":"0.0.54","date":"2026-10-26","lede":"Studio licence server, compact right-click menu with your own quick actions, timer-dial undo strip","highlights":["Studio licence server","Edit placement and Recenter for clay objects"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.54","items":[{"g":"n","t":"Studio licence server","b":"A studio can share a pool of seats across its network from one licence server. Each workstation takes a seat while Klay is open and returns it when Klay closes; when no seat is free, the panel lists who holds them.","w":["Settings \u203a Licence \u203a Studio server"]},{"g":"n","t":"Edit placement and Recenter for clay objects","b":"Edit placement shows a box around the clay volume. Move, rotate and resize it with the gizmo, the corner handles and the arrows on its edges, then Apply: the clay stays in place and is resampled into the box, finer when the box is smaller. Recenter object moves the sculpt to the middle of its volume without moving it in the scene.","w":["Right-click a clay object \u203a Edit placement"]},{"g":"n","t":"Live preview in Projection","b":"With Live preview on, the transfer is shown on the target before you press Project and updates when a setting or the source changes. Paint a mask on the target to hold areas back; the preview updates when the stroke ends. Project keeps the result, Cancel removes it.","w":["Right-click a mesh \u203a Projection \u203a Live preview"],"k":["[P]"]},{"g":"i","t":"A compact right-click menu","b":"The object menu now shows one row per category, with the verbs of each in a side menu, so it fits on screen. A row of quick actions sits at the top: right-click one to choose the function it holds, from this menu or from the app functions of the sidebar rail. Create gathers everything you can add, sculpt layers included, and Export gains Export all.","w":["Right-click an object"]},{"g":"i","t":"Undo strip reads like a dial","b":"The quick undo strip is now a sliding scale of step marks with numbers, the current step lit in the highlight colour. It keeps the same spacing at any history length; drag, flick, click a mark or use the wheel.","w":["Settings \u203a Undo \u203a Quick undo strip"],"k":["[Ctrl Z]"]},{"g":"i","t":"Brush value drag can be rebound","b":"The right-drag that sets brush size and strength is now a shortcut. It can take a modifier or a key on the right button, or be turned off.","w":["Settings \u203a Shortcuts \u203a Tools \u203a Brush value drag"]},{"g":"i","t":"Reduce a clay object from the menu","b":"Reduce, the opposite of Subdivide, now sits next to it in the clay object menu and makes the clay coarser. Its shortcut is Shift F; the minus key still works.","w":["Right-click a clay object \u203a Reduce"],"k":["[Shift F]"]},{"g":"f","t":"The Default button of the Projection dialog now also restores the hidden clean-up settings, so a projection that came out soft gets its full detail back."},{"g":"f","t":"Retopology on a mesh with UVs, such as the starter head, no longer tears the open edges or stalls on a growing count of parts. UV seams are now ignored."},{"g":"f","t":"After cancelling Retopology, pressing Retopo again starts a new run once the previous one has stopped."},{"g":"f","t":"The Polygroups tool's Shape, Act on selection and Reach tiles lost their labels at some UI scales."},{"g":"f","t":"Picking a face with the gizmo's Align button no longer crashes Klay on Windows."},{"g":"f","t":"Rebuild subdivision on a mesh with UVs no longer splits the mesh open along its UV seams on the lower levels."},{"g":"f","t":"Submenus of the outliner's right-click menu now open beside the menu instead of on top of it."},{"g":"f","t":"With orbit set to the right button, right-drag over the model now orbits in Armature, Bones, Lantern, Laser, Crop, Measure, Fields and Deformer; the tool keeps the click only on its own handles."}]},{"version":"0.0.53","date":"2026-10-25","lede":"The Flood tab, an Export and Import dialog with sculpt layers as blendshapes, a plane lock with a Plane Trim brush, Crumble for carving strokes, a Twist operator for ribbons and folds, faster async subdivision on the graphics card, polygroups with their own tool card and a source picker that survive remeshing, seamless textures and resized copies from the library, and a tangent-space normal map in the Baker.","highlights":["Flood tab","Export and Import dialog","Gizmo symmetry","Plane lock","Crumble","Twist"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.53","items":[{"g":"n","t":"Flood tab","b":"The Flood tab, in the sidebar's Sculpt group beside Layers and Brush, applies a stack of processes to the whole of the selected polygon mesh, on its current level, with a live preview: Bend, Twist, Taper, Inflate, Smooth, Polish, Clay polish, Noise, Displace texture and more than 20 others. A card at the top shows the mesh it works on, with the same thumbnail as in the outliner, its vertex count and its level, which can be changed from there. Clay polish flattens the surface into planar facets with crisp edges, with a facet angle and sharpness to set how faceted it gets; its Trim style cuts the surface into large flat planes of a chosen size, like the Trim brush, and its Strength goes up to 3. Noise offers 17 of the app's surface patterns, from grunge and veins to marble, wood grain, rust and scales, with their own contrast, warp and stretch controls. The stack is a list of processes read like layers, each with its icon, its main values, a full-width opacity slider and an on/off switch: the top process runs last, a new one is added on top, and a line is reordered by dragging it. A stack opacity in Output fades the whole stack at once. The selected process opens below the list with its settings, its axis, pivot, mask and symmetry, and a falloff curve along the axis. A process's mask can also be one of the Mask tool's presets, such as Cavity, Curvature or Height; it is recomputed on the shape the process receives, so it follows the processes above it. Apply stack keeps the stack and pauses Live preview, and Apply this switches that process off; Clear empties the stack.","w":["Flood"]},{"g":"n","t":"Export and Import dialog","b":"File > Export, the outliner\u2019s Export selected and Export group, and the export shortcut open one dialog with a tile for every format: OBJ, FBX, GLB, glTF, PLY, DAE, ABC, STL, Maya ASCII and Klay scene. A single pill chooses the whole scene or the selection. On a mesh with sculpt layers, FBX and glTF write the layers as blendshapes and Maya ASCII as a blendShape node, either every layer or a picked set. Formats without blendshapes bake the layers as shown, or also write one file per layer.","w":["File \u203a Export\u2026"]},{"g":"n","t":"Gizmo symmetry","b":"With Symmetry on in the Gizmo tool card and symmetry enabled, moving, rotating or scaling a mesh also applies the mirrored transform to its twin: a separate mesh with the same polygon count at the mirrored position, such as the second eye. One undo restores both.","w":["Toolbar \u203a Gizmo \u203a Symmetry"]},{"g":"n","t":"Plane lock","b":"With a polygon brush, hold R over the model to place a plane on the surface under the cursor; the brush switches to Plane Trim, which shaves only what lies above the plane down to it and leaves everything below untouched, and returns to the previous brush when the plane is turned off. Any other polygon brush chosen while the plane is on stops when it reaches the plane. Keep holding R and move the mouse to tilt the plane; hold R and drag with the right button, or turn the mouse wheel, to move it up or down along its normal. Drag the handle at the tip of the plane's stem to slide it, with Shift to snap and Ctrl for fine steps. A quick tap of R turns the last plane on or off without moving it.","w":["Brush \u203a Polygon \u203a R"]},{"g":"n","t":"Crumble","b":"With Crumble on, a polygon brush that carves, such as Scrape or a brush used with Ctrl, lands part of the removed clay back on the model as small sharp crumbs that pile up in front of the stroke, with a few on the groove's rims. Yield sets how much of the carved clay returns, Front bias how much of it gathers where the stroke goes, and Speed boost adds more crumbs to a faster stroke up to the speed set by Full at speed. The crumbs are made from noise or from a texture, and pen pressure can drive their yield, size and density.","w":["Brush \u203a Stamp & Falloff \u203a Crumble"]},{"g":"n","t":"Twist","b":"The Twist weight in Operator Blend now turns a polygon brush's Draw deposit as the stroke goes. The clay is laid as a side profile drawn in the Twist card, which can fold back over itself, and leans around the stroke, which makes ribbons, folds, waves and braided strands. The weight sets its strength, and a negative weight, or holding Ctrl, gives the mirror image of the shape across the stroke, still raised; Rhythm sets how the angle changes along the stroke. Strength, spacing and build-up act on it as they do on Draw, Smooth on the same brush softens the wave and the profile, and a later pass of the same stroke lies over the earlier one. A Twist brush preset is included.","w":["Brush \u203a Operator Blend \u203a Twist"]},{"g":"n","t":"Tangent-space normal map in the Baker","b":"The Baker can bake a tangent-space normal map from a multires mesh that reads correctly in Blender, Maya, Unreal and Substance. Frame selects Low mesh, for a model rendered without subdivision, or Subdivided low, for use together with a displacement map. Flip green switches the map to the DirectX convention.","w":["Baker \u203a Normal (tangent)"]},{"g":"n","t":"Make seamless","b":"Right-click a texture in the library and choose Process > Make seamless to open it in the viewer with a Seamless card. The picture is shown tiled, with the seams drawn and a before and after split, and updates as the settings change. Cut + Heal follows natural edges such as mortar or cracks, Soft blend suits sand, grass and moss, and Fill rebuilds the seam from the rest of the picture.","w":["Library \u203a Process \u203a Make seamless"]},{"g":"n","t":"Resize copies","b":"Process > Resize copies writes smaller copies of the selected pictures at the standard sizes from 16K down to 256, or at half or a quarter of each file. The resolution in a file name, such as 8k, 4K or 4096, is replaced with the new size in the same style, or added when the name has none, and a table lists every file before it is written.","w":["Library \u203a Process \u203a Resize copies"]},{"g":"n","t":"Brush accessibility","b":"An Accessibility card at the bottom of the Brush tab marks what a clay or polygon brush was made for. A brush marked VR is shown greyed out on the monitor, with a Balanced for VR tooltip, and can still be used. A polygon brush marked Poly only is greyed out while a clay layer is selected, and its strokes are not applied to clay.","w":["Brush \u203a Accessibility"]},{"g":"i","t":"One Boolean panel for clay and polygons","b":"Blend is now part of Boolean. Boolean in the outliner, or the Boolean shortcut, on clay objects opens the same Boolean panel as on polygon meshes, with the clay live in the viewport. The fourth operation is Extract, and a Join section sets the profile of the seam: Round, Chamfer, Muscle, Groove, Weld or Inflate, each with its own sliders and curve. Apply, Enter or D applies; Close or Esc cancels. The sidebar no longer changes to a Blend card, and D still merges selected clay at once.","w":["Outliner \u203a Boolean"]},{"g":"i","t":"Right-drag sets brush size and strength","b":"Right-dragging on a brush changes its size (left and right) or its strength (up and down), like holding B or M. A right-click without moving still opens the viewport menu, and the Mask brush keeps right-drag to erase. The Move and Elastique twist is now Ctrl + right-drag, as on the polygon Grab brush.","w":["Viewport \u203a Sculpting"]},{"g":"i","t":"Import size and position","b":"The Import model dialog now offers four sizes: Original, Match scene, Fit this file and, for several files, Fit each, which gives every model the same size at the centre. Position sets where the model lands in any size: Keep, Centre or On ground. Up axis turns the model as it comes in: Z up for files from 3ds Max or CAD, Flip Y\u00b7Z for a ZBrush OBJ that arrives upside-down. Original also takes a file unit, such as cm or m. Export turns the model back and restores the file's size and position.","w":["File \u203a Import"]},{"g":"i","t":"Faster strokes on large polygon meshes","b":"Strokes on large polygon meshes no longer slow down with the brush size, and run at about twice the frame rate in Unlit.","w":["Viewport \u203a Sculpting"]},{"g":"i","t":"Async subdivision, much faster","b":"Subdivide now runs on the graphics card and is much faster, especially at high levels.","w":["Outliner \u203a Subdivide"]},{"g":"i","t":"Retopology keeps polygroups","b":"Keep polygroups, in both Smooth and Sharp, places edge loops on the borders of the mesh's polygroups and gives the new mesh the same polygroups, with their names and colours. It replaces Follow polygroups, which was available in Smooth only and did not carry the polygroups over.","w":["Outliner \u203a Retopology"]},{"g":"i","t":"Mist in a box","b":"Edit in the Mist section shows the universal gizmo on the mist, which now sits in a box with soft edges: move it, rotate it to tilt the layer, and scale it to set its width and depth. Scaling it vertically sets the Thickness. Edge softness controls how gradually it fades at the sides, and the Box toggle returns to the endless floor layer.","w":["Lighting \u203a Volumetric \u203a Mist"]},{"g":"i","t":"Tessellation indicator","b":"While brush tessellation is on, a Tessellation indicator beside the sidebar shows the brush's mode, Densify or Adaptive, with a dot in that mode's colour. Its X turns tessellation off. The toolbar no longer changes colour.","w":["Viewport \u203a Sculpting"]},{"g":"i","t":"Sidebar tabs in groups, view buttons inside the panel","b":"The sidebar's tabs are arranged in five groups at the top of the panel: Sculpt, Surface, Stage, Output and App. The selected group shows its name, and a second row lists its tabs side by side. Each group returns to the tab last used in it, and the mouse wheel over the header steps through the tabs. The Post Processing tab is renamed Filter.","w":["Sidebar"]},{"g":"i","t":"Polygroups","b":"Zones are renamed Polygroups. A mesh card's Polygroups segment lists each set and its polygroups, and New set builds a set from the painted mask, UV shells, UDIM tiles, islands, angle, curvature, normal direction, symmetry, vertex colour and other sources. A selected polygroup can be grown, shrunk, relaxed or smoothed with a live preview, then inverted, merged, split, moved to a new mesh, masked, hidden or deleted, from the list, a right-click or the pastille beside the sidebar. Every entry of a polygroup's right-click menu has an icon. Copy takes the selected polygroups, and Paste, on a polygroup or a set, adds them to that set as new polygroups on the same faces, including onto another mesh with the same topology. The preview stays live while the view is limited to the selection, and the pastille's Mask masks the selected polygroups.","w":["Outliner \u203a Polygroups"]},{"g":"i","t":"Split dialog","b":"The Split dialog shows its main choices at the top: Islands or Polygroups, with the number of each and the mesh's polygroup sets, then Largest, Pick or All. Pick starts with nothing selected. In the viewport, a click selects or drops a part, dragging across parts selects them, and dragging from empty space draws a rectangle or a lasso; Shift adds and Ctrl removes. Invert is a switch that keeps the unselected parts. Select similar adds every part close to the last one clicked, by polygon count, bounding box or both, within a tolerance. Display shows the parts the split removes, ghosts them as see-through, or hides them. Cleanup can delete every part smaller than a percentage of the mesh's bounding box. Result holds Group parts, Compact and Keep original, which leaves a hidden copy of the mesh. Each section folds on its chevron. A new Delete button removes the selected parts and leaves the rest of the mesh in place.","w":["Outliner \u203a Split loose parts"]},{"g":"i","t":"Select tool: loops, hover and gizmo","b":"In Face mode a quad model selects whole quads, and the selection keeps full detail when the camera zooms out.","w":["Toolbar \u203a Select"]},{"g":"i","t":"Faster library with previews and multiple selection","b":"The library keeps small copies of its pictures in a thumbnails folder of the Klay user folder, so it opens faster and loads only the pictures near the visible part of the list. Only that part of the list is built, so a library of thousands of pictures scrolls smoothly. Moving the window and scrolling, including dragging the list with the left or middle button, are smoother: the mouse wheel glides and accelerates on fast turns, and on macOS the trackpad scrolls the list directly under the fingers and keeps coasting after they lift.
